model_policy: No call in this experiment uses a Fable model (owner, 2026-10-15): arms, nested calls, in-process subagents, judges and every coordination, authoring and review subagent. Allowed Claude answering models: claude-opus-5-5 (planner, Claude judge, guard default, subagent pin) and claude-sonnet-5-5 (reviewed_change coder); OpenAI models gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6-sol through Codex. The scan records Fable hits per run and judge. The controller's evidence-only census (eb3/model_census.py, standard library, reusing scan.claude_sessions and scan.answering_model) records answering-model counts per run tree and judge directory, metadata only. Its sweep lists -tmp- project sessions written in the batch window with session id, mtime, cwd and model counts only, and attributes one to a run only when its /tmp/<rel> cwd exists under exactly one E-B3 tree's tmp/ and not on the host /tmp; every other such session is reported unattributed (host sessions default to Fable, so they are expected and only counted). A session started by an absolute CLI path or a reset PATH outside /tmp and outside a tree is invisible to both scan and sweep
hidden_acceptance: descriptive only. The existing summarize.py --python /home/ollie/miniconda3/bin/python computes it for every clone, as before. No hidden measure has a threshold, gates validity, ranks, selects or excludes a run, judge or batch, or bears on a verdict. verdict_rules: Each claim is judged separately. A claim is 'not evaluated' if any of its <arm>.runs entries is not met or not emitted; otherwise it holds iff all its other entries are met, and a measure summarize does not emit counts as not met. Secondary entries and every hidden or per-judge figure never change a verdict; a gain of exactly 0 is neither positive nor negative. A claim that holds is a directional observation by two LLM judges on three runs per arm of one task, not a significance test, a population estimate or a measure of correctness.
validity: Void unless: mapping.json's task is <runtime>/<task>; the package hash matches at runtime.commit; its judges equal `judges`; every batch carries exactly the `anchors` stems; every counted judge's scoring run binds this file's sha256, and mapping.json's criterion_sha256 equals it; mapping.json's runtime_commit and every pooled run's record.json runtime_commit equal runtime.commit (checked by the controller); mapping.json's runs are exactly records/<arm>/run-1..run-3 under work_root for the three arms; every pooled run's tree and every counted judge's directory holds .model-guard/claude byte-identical to <runtime>/experiments/compare/shim/model-guard; and no pooled run and no counted judge has a Fable-model hit or an attributed Fable sweep session. Hidden acceptance is not a validity condition.
anchor_use: Anchor judge scores and hidden fractions are reported per batch and judge only; nothing is adjusted, excluded, rescaled or re-scored because of them, and neither gates validity.
judge_rules: Judge scores are the primary measure. summarize needs at least one judge to emit any measure (a run with no judge score has no value and is not counted in <arm>.runs). A judge is left out only by a contaminated scan verdict or a Fable-model hit recorded, with its reason, before summarize; with one left the verdict uses that judge, the report says so, and the thresholds' one-judge lattice applies; with none, summarize refuses and both claims are not evaluated. A judge stopped by a provider failure is resumed (R38), never re-run. Judges, bindings and score.orc's prompt are unchanged.
threshold_provenance: Chosen by the coordinator before any scoring or outcome readout. The owner selected the existing blind rubric. DRE's +1 point is an aggregate difference equivalent to one ordinal step in one of the four 0-2 rubric criteria, out of 8. RC's +0.5 mean and no-negative-run rule is reused unchanged from E-A's frozen criterion for continuity; E-A disclosed that its origin was a threshold set below September's observed +0.58, which had not been preregistered. Neither threshold is a power calculation or statistical-significance claim. Historical E-B2 instrument observations (not calibrated performance evidence) show moderate inter-judge agreement and substantial disagreement, so per-judge values and anchor ratings are reported.

thresholds.chosen_by: the coordinator, prospectively, after the owner's reply and before any score exists; not an explicit owner answer
thresholds.design_review_execute: human rule: the arm's mean blind score is at least 1 point (of 8) above the control's. Written >= 0.9: with two judges a clone score is a multiple of 1/2, so with exactly three valued runs per arm the difference of arm means is a multiple of 1/6 (one judge: 1/3); the values next to 1 are 5/6 and 2/3, both below 0.9, while float error in a difference of two means (about 1e-15) could put an exact 1 just under 1.0
thresholds.reviewed_change: human rule, as E-A: the mean paired gain (final minus first patch's blind score) is at least 0.5, and no run's gain is negative. Written >= 0.5 exactly: each run's gain is a multiple of 1/2 (two judges) or 1 (one judge), and statistics.mean of three such values is correctly rounded, so a true 0.5 is computed as 0.5; with one judge the reachable values next to 0.5 are 1/3 and 2/3
thresholds.run_floors: <arm>.runs >= 3 for every arm a claim uses, unchanged
thresholds.fixed: before any pool, judge score or hidden result; never adjusted after results

judge_reporting: per judge: each arm's mean total, design_review_execute's and reviewed_change's minus_control, and reviewed_change's paired gain per run and mean, computed from results.json clones.<id>.ratings (summarize's clone-id join) as E-B2's per-judge columns were; for each claim the report states whether its primary entries would be met under each judge alone. Reported prominently, never used for a verdict.
